articles.title: An analysis of risk factors for failure after operative treatment of displaced femoral neck fractures in patients 18-60 years of age.
articles.authors: Roddy E, Rockov Z, Firoozabadi R
articles.population: Patients aged 18-60 years who underwent operative fixation of a displaced femoral neck fracture
articles.outcomes: Treatment failure defined as femoral neck nonunion, fixation failure, avascular necrosis, or malunion. Overall failure rate was 30% (nonunion/fixation failure 13%, avascular necrosis 19%, malunion 5%)
articles.take_home: In younger adults treated for displaced femoral neck fractures, about 3 in 10 experience treatment failure. The risk is higher with greater initial fracture displacement, use of cannulated screws instead of fixed-angle implants, and if the fracture reduction is good rather than excellent.

articles.title: Uncorrected Preoperative Malnutrition Is Associated with Worse Outcomes After Operative Fixation of Diaphyseal Tibial Fractures.
articles.authors: Pereira DE, McCoy L, Harrison NJ, Bushe K, Kotzur T, McAndrew C, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients aged 18 years and over undergoing fixation of tibial shaft fractures
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications including nonunion, revision surgery, infection, failure of fixation, thromboembolic events, and sepsis
articles.take_home: Patients who were malnourished before tibial fracture surgery had significantly higher rates of complications like infection, nonunion and need for further surgery. Correcting malnutrition after surgery reduced some complications, though infection and revision surgery risks remained higher than in patients who were well-nourished from the start.

articles.title: Functional Outcomes Following Bipolar Hip Hemiarthroplasty via the Direct Anterior Approach Versus Posterior and Direct Lateral Approaches: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Yen Yu TS, Poh Hwee NJ, Xiaoe Z, Leng TT
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years and older with displaced femoral neck fractures undergoing bipolar hip hemiarthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 504 patients identified (400 posterior approach, 79 direct anterior approach, 25 direct lateral approach); 67 direct anterior and 134 posterior approach cases analysed after matching
articles.outcomes: Modified Barthel Index and Parker Mobility Score at discharge, 6 months and 12 months; length of hospital stay; postoperative complications; reoperation; and 1-year mortality
articles.take_home: The direct anterior approach led to slightly better early recovery at hospital discharge compared to the posterior approach, but this difference disappeared by 12 months. By one year, both approaches showed similar functional recovery, hospital stay length and survival rates.

articles.title: Preoperative High-Sensitivity Troponin and Risk of In-Hospital Mortality and Cardiac Events after Hip Fracture Surgery.
articles.authors: Toure AS, Okafor K, Medilien B, Mather R, Parry J, Hernandez-Irizarry RC, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing hip fracture surgery with preoperative high-sensitivity cardiac troponin measurement
articles.outcomes: In-hospital cardiac events, in-hospital mortality, and composite outcome of cardiac event or mortality
articles.take_home: Patients with elevated heart enzyme levels before hip fracture surgery had a higher risk of heart problems and death during their hospital stay. Those with the highest enzyme levels (above 100 ng/L) faced the greatest risk, regardless of how soon they had surgery.

articles.title: Cumulative traumatic life events and increased risk for emergency department and inpatient utilization after physical injury hospitalization.
articles.authors: Huynh M, O'Connor S, McManamen M, Buggaveeti AE, Russo J, Wang J, et al.
articles.study_type: Secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial
articles.population: Adults aged 18 and over hospitalized for physical injury with screening for elevated posttraumatic stress symptoms
articles.outcomes: Emergency department and inpatient visits in the 12 to 36 months following index injury admission
articles.take_home: People who experienced multiple serious traumatic events before their injury, or who had traumatic events in the year after their injury, were more likely to need emergency department or hospital visits in the following 1 to 3 years. Those with 7 or more prior traumatic events, previous emergency department visits, lower education, or traumatic events after their injury all showed increased healthcare use.

articles.title: Automated impaction in uncemented total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Brkljac M, Bandeira E, Sharma S, Guevel B, Cobb J, Logishetty K
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary uncemented total hip replacement
articles.sample_size: 2,607 hip replacements across five studies (2,377 in meta-analysis)
articles.outcomes: Risk of intraoperative periprosthetic femoral fractures and operating time
articles.take_home: Automated impaction systems did not reduce the risk of femoral fractures or reduce operating time compared with manual impaction during hip replacement. The risk of fracture and efficiency may depend more on how well the implant fits the individual patient's bone.

articles.title: Association between surgically treated knee injury and knee arthroplasty: an explorative study based on Finnish nationwide register-based data.
articles.authors: Heikkila O, Sund R, Kroger H, Jaroma A, Sirola J
articles.population: Finnish residents aged 15-99 years who had knee injury surgery between 1986 and 2024, compared with those without knee injury diagnosis or treatment
articles.sample_size: 2,163 knee replacements in fracture surgery group; 13,570 in non-fracture injury surgery group; 205,440 in control group
articles.outcomes: Incidence of knee replacement surgery, stratified by age, sex and injury type
articles.take_home: People who have knee surgery for injuries are more likely to need a knee replacement later, with the biggest increase in those aged 15-54 years. Those who had non-fracture knee injuries were at higher risk than those with fracture injuries.

articles.title: Upper-limb physical activity after distal radius fractures treated operatively or nonoperatively: a secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized trial.
articles.authors: Tonning LU, Hevonkorpi TP, Launonen AP, Reito A, Skjaerbaek MS, Luokkala T, et al.
articles.study_type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized controlled trial
articles.population: Adults with malaligned distal radius fractures treated operatively or nonoperatively, plus healthy older adults for comparison
articles.sample_size: 157 patients with fractures and 59 healthy controls
articles.outcomes: High-intensity upper-limb activity measured by wrist-worn accelerometers at 3 and 12 months
articles.take_home: Patients who had surgery for malaligned wrist fractures were more active in their injured arm at 12 months than those treated without surgery, with activity levels similar to healthy older adults. Those treated without surgery remained less active than healthy people at 12 months.

articles.title: Dual mobility versus standard cups in total hip replacement for displaced femoral neck fractures (Duality): an international, multicentre, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
articles.authors: Hailer NP, Griffin XL, Mukka S, Lakic TG, Appelbe D, Skoldenberg O, et al.
articles.population: People aged 65 years or older with a displaced femoral neck fracture treated with total hip replacement
articles.outcomes: Dislocation of the hip joint within 1 year requiring closed reduction or open surgery
articles.take_home: Dual mobility hip replacements reduced dislocation rates to 1.3% compared with 4.2% for standard replacements in older patients with femoral neck fractures. This substantial reduction means dual mobility replacements are recommended for this group of patients.

articles.title: A Comprehensive Guide to Tibial Nailing Systems for Short Segment Nailing Procedures.
articles.authors: Khalafallah YM, Morrow BA, Dirschl DR
articles.population: Tibial intramedullary nail systems marketed in the United States
articles.outcomes: Interlocking screw configurations, nail diameter, total length, and design features across systems
articles.take_home: This study compared 13 different tibial nail systems available in the UK to help surgeons choose the right implant for short segment fracture fixation. The systems varied in their design features, with differences in the number and position of interlocking screws and available nail sizes.

articles.title: Minimally Invasive Screw Fixation of Olecranon Fractures.
articles.authors: Folberg CR, Zimerman T, Andre de Oliveira Alves J, Sirena Pereira FM, Galia CR
articles.population: Adults with closed olecranon fractures (Mayo type IA, IB, IIA or IIB)
articles.outcomes: Mayo Elbow Performance Score, elbow range of motion, complications including infection and hardware failure
articles.take_home: Minimally invasive screw fixation for certain olecranon fractures produced good or excellent results in 30 of 31 patients, with most patients recovering more than 100 degrees of elbow movement and very few complications or infections.

articles.title: Surgical Fixation Enhances Discharge Independence in Elderly Patients With Fragility Fractures of the Pelvis.
articles.authors: Quercetti NF, DiStefano S, Yayac M, Mastrokostas PG, Getchell J, Ng MK
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years and older with fragility fractures of the pelvis from low-energy mechanisms
articles.sample_size: 132 patients (56 nonoperative, 55 acute fixation, 21 delayed fixation)
articles.outcomes: Pain scores (VAS), hospital length of stay, in-hospital and 90-day complications, discharge destination
articles.take_home: Elderly patients who had surgery for fragility pelvic fractures were more likely to go home rather than to hospital discharge to a care facility, compared to those treated without surgery. Pain relief was similar between surgical and non-surgical treatment groups.

articles.title: Effect of prior rotator cuff repair technique and timing on clinical outcomes of reverse shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Holt KE, Hao KA, Bindi VE, Kaiser AHA, Hones KM, Wright JO, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected database
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse shoulder arthroplasty after previous rotator cuff repair
articles.outcomes: American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score, forward elevation, and external rotation at minimum two-year follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients who had arthroscopic rotator cuff repair before their reverse shoulder arthroplasty had better shoulder function and movement than those who had open repair. Waiting longer between the initial repair and the reverse shoulder arthroplasty was also associated with better outcomes.

articles.title: Incidence of medical and surgical complications, and subsequent mortality, after hip fracture surgery : a nationwide cohort study from 2010 to 2021.
articles.authors: Haugen KG, Hansen CM, Jensen SS, Pedersen AB
articles.population: Hip fracture patients aged 65 years and over who underwent surgery
articles.outcomes: 30-day cumulative incidence of medical and surgical complications; mortality within 31 to 60 days after surgery
articles.take_home: Medical complications occurred in 23% of hip fracture patients and surgical complications in 4%, with pneumonia and urinary tract infections being most common. Patients who experienced any complication had three times higher mortality compared to those without complications.

articles.title: Primary total hip arthroplasty after prior osteosynthesis versus osteotomy : distinct risk profiles and the modifying effect of femoral fixation.
articles.authors: Wagener N, Wu Y, Perka C, Hardt S
articles.study_type: Comparative cohort study using registry data
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip replacement, with or without prior hip surgery (either bone fixation or bone reshaping)
articles.sample_size: 8,643 matched pairs (prior fixation versus none) and 5,569 matched pairs (prior reshaping versus none)
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery, periprosthetic femoral fracture, infection, dislocation, and loosening
articles.take_home: Patients who had prior bone fixation surgery need cemented or hybrid hip replacements to reduce fracture and revision risks, whereas those with prior bone reshaping surgery have different risks mainly involving dislocation and loosening. These two groups should be assessed separately before surgery rather than treated the same way.

articles.title: Hospital costs attributable to further fracture, reoperation, and death during the first year following hip fracture in England : a nationwide cohort study.
articles.authors: Baji P, Gregson CL, Patel R, Judge A, Chesser T, Griffin XL, et al.
articles.study_type: Nationwide cohort study using linked national datasets
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years and over who had hip fracture surgery in English hospitals
articles.outcomes: Inpatient hospital costs during the first year after hip fracture, associated with further fractures, reoperations, and death
articles.take_home: Patients who had further fractures or needed another operation after their initial hip fracture surgery had roughly double the hospital costs compared to those with no complications. Complications and deaths accounted for about a third of all hip fracture patients but used over half of the total money spent on hip fracture care nationally.

articles.title: The management of distal humeral fractures in older patients.
articles.authors: Yoong AWH, Super JT, Tan GJS, Watts AC, Ollivere BJ, Duckworth AD
articles.population: Older adults with distal humeral fractures
articles.outcomes: Functional outcomes, reoperation rates, complications including infection, nonunion, instability and loosening
articles.take_home: Treatment options for broken bones at the bottom of the upper arm in older people include non-surgical management, surgery to repair the bone, or replacement of the elbow joint. Recent studies suggest that surgery to repair the bone and elbow replacement give similar results in the short to medium term, although surgery to repair the bone may need more repeat operations.

articles.title: The Manitoba Joint Replacement Registry: validation of a provincial hip and knee arthroplasty registry.
articles.authors: Poitras C, Righolt CH, Bohm ER
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and over who underwent hip or knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Completeness and accuracy of registry data compared with hospital discharge and medical services databases; percentage agreement and Cohen's kappa scores
articles.take_home: The Manitoba Joint Replacement Registry has high-quality data that can be reliably used for research and quality improvement, with coverage improving from 68% in 2008 to 97% by 2023. However, some rural hospitals captured fewer hip fracture procedures than elective operations.

articles.title: Trauma nursing as frontline health diplomacy: A binational ATCN program for Palestinian and Israeli nurses during conflict.
articles.authors: Jreis T, Kruyer VN, Kaim A, Becker D, Hani W, Mohammed A, et al.
articles.study_type: Educational intervention study with questionnaire evaluation
articles.population: Palestinian and Israeli trauma nurses
articles.outcomes: Course satisfaction (mean 8.44/10), perceived educational impact (mean 4.39/5), interest in maintaining professional contact (94.4%), correlation between belief in cooperation improving care and positive health-diplomacy attitudes (rs=.74, p<.001)
articles.take_home: Joint trauma nursing training courses for Palestinian and Israeli nurses were highly valued by participants and strongly supported the idea that professional cooperation improves patient care. Participants reported high satisfaction with the training and most wanted to continue working together professionally.

articles.title: Agreement between ChatGPT and emergency physicians in laceration management: A prospective study.
articles.authors: Saglam Gurmen E, Yorgancioglu M, Oral A
articles.population: Patients with traumatic lacerations presenting to emergency department
articles.outcomes: Agreement between ChatGPT recommendations and emergency physicians' decisions on suture material, technique, suture count, wound classification and antibiotic use, measured using Cohen's kappa
articles.take_home: ChatGPT showed considerable to almost perfect agreement with emergency physicians' decisions on laceration management across all decision areas, with accuracy ranging from 82.6% to 91.7%. The study suggests ChatGPT could be used as a clinical decision-support tool in emergency medicine, though physician oversight remains essential.

articles.title: Variation in surgical indications across national distal radius fracture guidelines: A comparative review.
articles.authors: Oftebro I, Olsen B, Enger MM, Hassellund SS, Solberg LB
articles.population: Adults with dorsally displaced distal radius fractures
articles.outcomes: Variation in surgical indication thresholds across guidelines; differences in radiographic criteria, age-related modifications, and patient-related factors
articles.take_home: Different countries use different thresholds to decide whether to operate on broken wrists, which may lead to varying treatment rates and healthcare costs. The study found that guidelines agree on measuring certain fracture features but disagree on the exact thresholds for surgery, and there is a need for international agreement on clearer surgical criteria.

articles.title: Untreated ulnar styloid fractures do not compromise wrist function in patients with distal radius fractures: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Li C, Gao W, Yang C, Jia Z, Li J
articles.population: Patients with distal radius fractures, with and without untreated ulnar styloid fractures
articles.outcomes: Wrist function scores, grip strength, and wrist range of motion (flexion, extension, pronation, supination, ulnar and radial deviation)
articles.take_home: Leaving ulnar styloid fractures untreated does not harm wrist function in patients with distal radius fractures, whether in the short or long term. There was a small difference in function scores in the first 6 months, but this did not have clinical importance and disappeared after 6 months.

articles.title: Lateral epicondylar fractures in the pediatric population: Presentation, management, and outcomes.
articles.authors: Kushare I, Ghanta R, Smadi Z, Wunderlich N, Phillips T
articles.population: Children under 18 years with lateral epicondyle fractures
articles.outcomes: QuickDASH scores, time to return to activity, rates of stiffness, need for surgery
articles.take_home: Most children with lateral epicondyle fractures do well with immobilisation in a cast for about 4 weeks. However, doctors need to check carefully for other injuries at the same time, as these may need surgery.

articles.title: Prosthetic leg socket design: New insight on different tibia length and distal bevelled angle using finite element analysis.
articles.authors: Baharuddin MH, Abdullah NNAA, Kori MI, Gan HS, Abdul Kadir MR, Ramlee MH
articles.population: Single volunteer with lower limb amputation
articles.outcomes: Stress distribution on soft tissue of residual limb with different tibial lengths (12.5 cm, 15 cm, 17.5 cm), distal tibial bevelling angles (30°, 45°, 60°), and soft tissue stiffness values
articles.take_home: Using computer modelling, researchers found that for this individual patient, a tibial length of 15 cm with a 45-degree bevelled angle and contracted soft tissue produced the best stress distribution in the residual limb, with no predicted pain during standing. The shape and length of the remaining bone after amputation significantly affects how pressure is distributed on the remaining leg tissue.

articles.title: Acute-phase hyperbaric oxygen therapy induces differential regulation of NF-kappaB/COX-2 and NLRP3 inflammasome pathways in traumatic brain injury.
articles.authors: Puspadewi M, Dewi S, Hardiany NS, Wiwoho YY, Jusuf AA, Satriotomo I, et al.
articles.population: Rats with induced traumatic brain injury
articles.outcomes: Brain inflammation markers (NF-kappaB, COX-2, NLRP3, caspase-1) and percentage of intact neurons measured on days 3, 7 and 14
articles.take_home: In rats, hyperbaric oxygen therapy given shortly after brain injury reduced some inflammatory markers and appeared to protect brain cells better than standard air treatment. These results are from laboratory animals and would need further research before use in patients.

articles.title: Comparison of three surgical methods in the treatment of displaced intra-articular calcaneal fractures: A retrospective study.
articles.authors: Zhao B, Ma C, Liu Q, Shen A, Du H, Li J, et al.
articles.population: Patients with displaced intra-articular calcaneal fractures (Sanders type II or III)
articles.outcomes: Radiological outcomes, AOFAS and VAS functional scores, intraoperative blood loss, weight-bearing time, complication rates
articles.take_home: Robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery had the best early recovery and lowest wound complications, whilst the extended lateral open approach had the highest wound complication rate, though all three methods produced similar long-term functional outcomes.

articles.title: Interpret with caution: randomized controlled trials comparing cemented versus press-fit hemiarthroplasty in geriatric patients with intracapsular hip fractures are statistically fragile.
articles.authors: Quinn M, Lou M, Morrissey P, Burstein E, Milner J, Evans AR, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Older patients with intracapsular hip fractures treated with hemiarthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Mortality, periprosthetic fracture, dislocation, and revision rates
articles.take_home: Many of the reported differences between cemented and press-fit hip replacements in older patients are statistically fragile, meaning small changes in patient numbers could reverse the findings. Results should be interpreted cautiously, particularly for mortality and complication rates.

articles.title: The management of pink pulseless hands in paediatric supracondylar humerus fractures: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Itte VN, Cowie J, Ali Yusuf Y, Zafar A, Wilson M, Jacob R, et al.
articles.population: Children with pink pulseless hands following supracondylar humerus fractures
articles.outcomes: Return of radial pulse within 24 hours, conversion to surgical exploration, long-term functional outcomes
articles.take_home: Surgical exploration restores the pulse more quickly than non-operative treatment alone, but long-term arm function is similar between the two approaches. Your child's doctor may try conservative management first, but should move to surgery promptly if the pulse does not return or there are other concerns.

articles.title: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery versus open thoracotomy for thoracic trauma in hemodynamically stable patients: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Barrientos ML, Zapata CAL, Lopez CAD
articles.population: Hemodynamically stable adults with thoracic trauma
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications, hospital stay, operative time, intraoperative blood loss, perioperative mortality, and conversion rate from VATS to thoracotomy
articles.take_home: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) resulted in fewer complications, shorter hospital stays, and shorter operating times compared with open thoracotomy in stable trauma patients, though the evidence quality is low and comes mainly from observational studies in China.

articles.title: Immersive virtual reality simulation for technical skills acquisition in pneumothorax management and chest tube insertion: A randomized controlled trial among surgery interns.
articles.authors: Leon S, Rouhi AD, Baji D, Goldberg DW, Hwang J, Weber D, et al.
articles.population: First-year surgery residents
articles.sample_size: 45 surgical residents (21 IVR group, 24 control group)
articles.outcomes: Technical skills measured by Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills (OSATS) score; performance in rib blunt dissection, economy of time and motion, and tutor assistance required
articles.take_home: Surgery trainees who learned chest tube insertion using immersive virtual reality headsets performed better on skills tests and needed less help from tutors than those taught using traditional classroom instruction. The virtual reality training was cost-effective and showed promise for wider use in surgical education.

articles.title: The use of blocking "screws" in retrograde intramedullary nailing for distal femur fractures: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Hallak A, Amzallag N, Zahalka S, Ben-Tov T, Khoury A
articles.population: Patients with distal femur fractures treated with retrograde intramedullary nailing
articles.outcomes: Postoperative alignment (coronal and sagittal malalignment), union rates, construct stability, complications
articles.take_home: Blocking screws used alongside retrograde intramedullary nailing consistently improved alignment in distal femur fractures, particularly in complex cases with comminution or wide canals, without affecting healing rates. Complications were uncommon and mainly involved minor hardware issues.
